rule:
An attribute-less `
` HTML tag in any spelling the parser produces (ASCII tag-name case-insensitive; zero or more space / tab / CR / LF before an optional `/`, so `
`, `
`, `
`, `
` and `` are all the same tag — whitespace AFTER the `/` is outside the grammar and never appears) that sits inside a `paragraph` / `heading` / `tableCell` phrasing subtree, and whose subtree contains NO OTHER raw `html` node, is normalized from an mdast `html` node into the canonical mdast `break` node (RENDERER_PIPELINE_VERSION 1.3.0+) — the same wire type `remark-breaks` already produces for a soft line break. A single non-bare `html` node ANYWHERE in that phrasing unit's subtree (an attribute, another tag, mixed text, a multi-tag value) blocks EVERY replacement in that unit, so a bare `
` sharing a unit with unrelated raw HTML stays `html`. Contamination is judged per `tableCell`, never per `tableRow`/`table` — one raw-HTML cell does not block its clean sibling cells. A bare `
` at FLOW position (a direct child of `root` / `blockquote` / `listItem`, not one of the 3 units above) is never touched.
why:
Non-web clients (RFC-0023 §4.1) treat `html` as opaque content and show a visible placeholder for it, even though an attribute-less `
` has a fully known meaning. `break` is an EXISTING v1 closed-registry type (`packages/api-contract/src/schemas/rendered-ast.ts`) that every native decoder already understands — this corpus fixes the NEW wire fact that `break` can now appear directly under `tableCell` (previously only possible under `paragraph` from `remark-breaks` or the GitHub Alerts marker delimiter), plus the producer-side contamination boundary that decides when a `
` is left as `html` instead. Pinning both the stored shape and the v1 envelope in the SAME case (not two independently-green halves) is what proves the producer (`core/break-normalization.ts`) and the projection (`sanitize-ast.ts`) agree on one wire contract.
consumerContract: The api jest driver asserts the PRODUCER side (markdown → expectedAst via runPipeline with an empty registry, and expectedAst → expectedEnvelope via sanitizeAst). The CrowiKit XCTest asserts the CONSUMER side (its sanitize-walker mirror over expectedAst, and its strict envelope decoder over expectedEnvelope). The Swift consumer is wired up in Phase 4 (apps/apple lives on the feature-ios-app/impl branch).
consumerCoordination: CrowiKit's production code needs NO change for this fixture: its envelope decoder already turns the wire discriminant `"break"` into `.lineBreak` (RenderedAstEnvelopeDecoder.swift), its parent-placement table already maps `"tableCell": (.tableCells, .phrasing)` matching this server's registry, its inline-text builder already renders `.lineBreak` as a real `"\n"`, and its table-cell view already renders that text with no `lineLimit`/`truncationMode`, so a `"\n"` becomes a real second line. The one required action is repo-mechanical, not a code change: the CrowiKit owner must add `"break-normalization"` to the hand-written `corpusFiles` array in `RenderedAstGoldenCorpusTests.swift` (currently `["core-blocks", "inline", "code", "image-attrs", "gfm-references", "typed-nodes"]`) before this fixture is ever read on that side — until then, `testEveryCorpusFileIsRegistered` on the CrowiKit side is what catches the omission (it fails loudly rather than silently skipping the new file).
exclusions:
Plugin-dispatch output byte strings (Mermaid / PlantUML / link-card / shiki generated HTML) are deliberately NOT pinned by this corpus — packages/e2e/tests/renderer-plugins.spec.ts owns that coverage against a live server. The web-rendered DOM parity between an `html("
")` tree and a `break` tree (same visual line break) is pinned by packages/web/src/components/editor/render-mdast.test.tsx instead, not here.

cases.name: table-cell-bare-br-normalized
cases.why:
positive — the central composite case: a single bare `
` inside a GFM table cell (`a
b`) normalizes to `break` in the stored AST, and the same `break` (not a placeholder) is what a declared v1 client receives inside `tableCell.children` — proving the producer (core/break-normalization.ts) and the projection (sanitize-ast.ts) agree on the same wire shape in one case rather than two independently-green halves.

cases.name: table-cell-multiple-br-normalized
cases.why:
positive — the most common real Crowi authoring pattern (multiple manual line breaks inside one table cell, `a
b
c`): both bare `
`s in the same clean unit convert to `break`, not just the first one.

cases.name: case-and-self-closing-variants-normalized
cases.why:
positive — the 3 accepted value forms (`
` / `
` / `
`) and ASCII tag-name case-insensitivity (`
` / `
`) all normalize inside an ordinary paragraph, with the surrounding text order preserved.

cases.name: whitespace-variants-normalized
cases.why:
CommonMark's open-tag grammar allows an unbounded whitespace run before the optional slash, so `
` / `
` / `` are the same attribute-less break as `
` and a reader cannot tell them apart. Pins that every spelling reaches non-web clients as a `break` rather than a placeholder — the narrower three-form set this transform originally accepted left the rest opaque.

cases.name: heading-bare-br-normalized
cases.why:
positive — headings are a phrasing unit too (registry `childModel: 'phrasing'`), so a heading whose only content is a bare `
` gets a `break` child on the wire even though it has no visible TOC label (core/headings.ts drops an HTML-only heading from the TOC, unrelated to this transform, and keeps stamping a non-empty anchor id from the raw text).

cases.name: whitespace-preserving-span-retained
cases.why:
negative — an author-built whitespace-preserving context (`x
y`): the unit's phrasing subtree holds 3 `html` nodes and only one of them is a bare `
`, so D-3's unit-scope contamination rule keeps ALL THREE as `html` (including the otherwise-bare `
`) rather than normalizing it and silently adding a visible extra line to this author-controlled whitespace context.

cases.name: table-cell-mixed-raw-html-retained
cases.why:
negative — a table cell mixing raw HTML with a bare `
` (`x
y`): the whole cell unit is contaminated by the non-bare ``/`` nodes, so the `
` also stays `html` and is transported as `html` (registry placement `both`) rather than `crowiOpaque`, matching today's opaque-HTML policy for non-web clients.

cases.name: flow-bare-br-retained
cases.why:
negative — a bare `
` with no enclosing paragraph/heading/tableCell (a standalone line) sits at FLOW position directly under `root`; break-normalization only ever touches phrasing-unit subtrees, so this stays `html` in both the stored AST and the v1 envelope — and, because `html` has registry placement `both`, it is valid there and never degrades to `crowiOpaque{reason:'invalid-position'}`.
